steps.cause: Regeneration valve in boom control valve
steps.procedure: 1. Release the pressure that remains in the hydraulic tank and piping to examine. For details, see Testing and Adjusting, “Release Remained Pressure in Hydraulic Circuit”. 2. Examine the control valve body and the boom regeneration valve to see if they are not twisted or stuck. (They must move smoothly and not be stuck.) Are they clean? REMARK Be careful that dirt does not enter during recovery work.

branches.YES: • Boom regeneration valve is normal. • Go to the next check item.
branches.NO: • Boom regeneration valve is defective. • Repair or replace the boom regeneration valve. • Go to “Confirmation of repair”.

steps.cause: Pressure compensation valve on RAISE side of boom control valve
steps.procedure: 1. Do relief of other work equipment and examine. 2. Is the boom stopped? 3. Stop the engine. 4. Release the pressure that remains in the hydraulic tank and piping. For details, see Testing and Adjusting, “Release Remained Pressure in Hydraulic Circuit”. 5. Interchange the pressure compensation valves on RAISE and LOWER sides of boom control valve, and examine. 6. Is there no change, and does the phenomenon reproduce? REMARK The area ratios of the pressure compensation valves on the RAISE and LOWER sides are different. Be sure to set them back to their initial positions after troubleshooting.

branches.YES: • Pressure compensation valve on RAISE side of boom control valve is normal. • Go to the next check item.
branches.NO: • Pressure compensation valve on RAISE side of boom control valve is defective. • Repair or replace the pressure compensation valve on RAISE side of boom control valve. • Go to “Confirmation of repair”.
